big_pour.headline: Major AI companies back shared scraping opt-out standard
big_pour.summary: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic will adopt a shared standard letting publishers set AI training preferences across multiple AI firms at once using a "policy token" signal.
big_pour.why: It gives publishers a single tool to decide whether AI companies can scrape their content.

explain.kid: Big AI companies agreed on a single stop sign that websites can show when they do not want their words taken.
explain.pm: Instead of configuring individual opt-outs per AI vendor, publishers can now use a single shared policy token to set training data permissions across major providers simultaneously.
explain.engineer: OpenAI, Google, Microsoft, and Anthropic are standardizing on a shared "policy token" signal, enabling publishers to declare AI training scraping preferences across multiple providers rather than managing individual crawler controls.

office_blend.summary: Worldwide Express used an Amazon Bedrock multi-agent system to cut active billing exceptions by 75%, improve time-to-cash by four weeks, and unlock $10 million in free cash flow.

office_blend.headline: Epsilon builds managed UI testing using Amazon Nova

word.definition: The cycle an agent repeats until it is done. The model decides on an action, code runs it, and the result goes back to the model to decide the next step.
word.heard: "Cap the agent loop at 10 steps so it can't run forever."
word.analogy: Like taste, adjust, taste again until the drink is right.
